newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT - TNT recommends KPN bid.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - TNT recommends KPN bid.

text.p: The following statement was issued by released by transport and logistics group TNT Ltd and Dutch Telecoms and Postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) detailing KPN's A$2.0 billion takeover bid for TNT and TNT's recommendation in favour of the bid.
KPN AND TNT CREATE A LEADER IN TIME SENSITIVE DISTRIBUTION AND LOGISTICS BY A RECOMMENDED CASH OFFER

The Boards of Royal PTT Nederland NV ("KPN"), the primary postal and telecommunications corporation in the Netherlands, and TNT Limited ("TNT"), the worldwide transport and logistics group based in Australia, announce that they have unanimously agreed recommended cash offers to be made by KPN for all of the shares of TNT (the "Offer").

This arrangement follows long-standing strategic discussions between KPN and TNT concerning the benefits to be gained from combing TNT's businesses with those of PTT Post BV ("PTT Post"), KPN's postal and logistics subsidiary, and their interests in GD Express Worldwide.
It will create a new global force in the time sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four worldwide.

KPN's offer values the whole of the fully diluted share capital of TNT at A$2.0 billion (NLG 2.7 billion), representing a premium of 48 percent over TNT's current market capitalisation (including both the ordinary and converting preference share capital).

The Directors of TNT unanimously recommend that shareholders in TNT accept KPN's offer, in the absence of a superior offer, as they intend to do in respect of all of their own shares and share options.
David Mortimer, Managing Director and Chief Executive of TNT, said today:

"This proposal represents an outstanding opportunity to create a strong global transportation group. For TNT shareholders, it delivers premium value. Today marks an important milestone in the development of our businesses over the past four years. KPN is a logical partner for our businesses and this is a winning proposal for both TNT and KPN. This transaction reflects the value we have created.
My fellow Directors and I unanimously recommend that TNT shareholders support this proposal by accepting KPN's offer".
Mr Wim Dik, Chairman of the Mangement Board and Chief Executive officer of KPN, said today:

"For KPN, this acquisition represents a significant step in our strategy to pursue growth annd international expansion of our core businesses. We have had a long and productive association with TNT through our joint venture in GD Express Worldwide.
"I am excited by the tremendous business opportunities which will result from the combination of the excellent operations within PTT Post, TNT and GD Express Worldwide."
Mr Ad Scheepbouwer, Chief Executive Officer of PTT Post and a member of the Board of Mangement of KPN, who will manage the combined worldwide operations, said today:
"This new group will allow PTT Post to broaden the scope of its activities from mainly domestic postal operations to worldwide time sensitive distribution and logistics.

"Our excellent revenue and profit record over recent years will provide a strong platform for the combined opertions. TNT has an outstanding multinational mangement team and valuable strategic positions around the world. Our combination will lead to significant operational and financial benefits, and the capacity to deliver a superior service to our customers."
BACKGROUND TO THE TRANSACTION

Since 1992, PTT Post and TNT have enjoyed a close commercial relationship due to their joint interest in GD Express Worldwide, the worldwide time sensitive distribution comapany. GD Express Worldwide trades under the brand name TNT Express Worldwide, serving more than 200 countries.
Swedish Posten has an indirect interest in GD Express Worldwide.

TNT and KPN have recognised the benefits to be gained from the combination of their respective time sensitive distribution and logistics operations within a number of countries around the world with the international network of GD Expres sWorldwide. Discussions on how to realise these benefits have led to the Offer being announced today.
This major transaction will combine the operations of:
- TNT's domestic time sensitive distribution and logistics businesses in the four largest European countries (Italy,Germany, UK and France), the Americas, Australia and Asia;
- PTT Post's domestic time sensitive distribution and logistics businesses within The Netherlands, Germany, Belgium, Austria and Denmark, as well as its interntional mail services; and
- TNT and PTT Post's international time sensitive services through their joint interest in GD Express Worldwide.

With a primary focus on Europe, the combined opertions will capitalise on the customer franchises and strong brand images of TNT and GD Express Worldwide (trading as TNT Express Worldwide) throughout the world.

Combining these operations will strengthen the existing businesses and provide a strong platform for growth in senistive distribution and logistics, particularly in the expanding European and Asian markets.
The combination will create a new integrated worldwide network capable of delivering a superior service to customers and strategically positioned to capitalise on future market opprotunities.
Ranking in the top four global leaders in this industry, the new group will:
- be number one in time sensitive distribution in Europe
- offer services in more than 200 countries with its own operations in 47 countries;
- have time sensitive distribution and logistics revenues of over A$6 billion (NLG 8 billion)
- carry a volume of more than two million time sensitive consignments a week with a total weight of 70 million kilogrammes;
- be one of the fastest growing European providers in the rapidly expanding logistics market;
- instantly become the largest international business mail service provider with a global presence; and
- have a solid platform inthe emerging Asian market.
DETAILS OF THE OFFER

KPN will make the following recommended cash offers under Australian takeover schemes for all of the ordinary and converting preference shares of TNT, including ordinary shares, if any, resulting from the conversion of convertible securities and the exercise of share options:

For each ordinary share A$2.45 per share in cash and for each converting preference share A$2.45 per share in cash plus 6.2 cent TNT dividend Holders of converting preference shares will receive the above dividend from TNT for the six month period ending 30th November, 1996.
Dividend cheques will be dispatched by TNT on 2nd December, 1996.
Converting preference shares will be acquired by KPN under the Offer together with all rights (if any) to dividends for the period beyond 30th November, 1996.

Financial benefits for TNT shareholders The Offer values the whole of the fully diluted share capital of TNT at A$2.0 billion (NLG 2.7 billion), a premium of 48 per cent, to the fully diluted market capitalisation of TNT on 1st October, 1996. The Offer represents a multiple of 10.6 times TNT's consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and abnormal items and 19.1 times TNT's consolidated earnings before interest, tax and abnormal items for the year ended 30th June, 1996, and a multiple of 2.6 times the consolidated fully diluted net assets per share of TNT as at 30th June, 1996.
The offer for the TNT ordinary shares of A$2.45 in cash per share constitutes a 50 per cent premium to the closing TNT ordinary share price on 1st October, 1996.

The offer for the TNT converting preference shares of A$2.45 in cash per share, combined with the 6.2 cents preference dividend which converting preference shareholders will receive from TNT for the period ending 30th November, 1996, represents a combined value of A$2.512 per share, a 41 per cent premium to the TNT converting preference share price on 1st October, 1996.
FINANCIAL BENEFITS FOR KPN SHAREHOLDERS
The acquisition of TNT will drive further earnings growth for KPN shareholders by moving resources of KPN into growing markets, improving geographic and sector spread.
KPN anticipates that the acquisition will be earnings positive in 1997 and thereafter, taking into account the net effect of the ongoing costs of the acquisition and the positive impact of synergies.

Management and employees Mr. Ad Scheepbouwer, Chief Executive Officer of PTT Post and a member of the Board of Management of KPN, will manage the combined worldwide operations of PTT Post, TNT and GD Express Worldwide.
Mr. David Mortimer, Managing Director and Chief Executive of TNT, has advised KPN that, based on the Offer being successful, he wishes to remain resident in Australia.

KPN has invited Mr. Mortimer to be Chairman and Chief Executive of the Australian and Asian operations of the combined PTT Post and TNT group, which will include responsibility for the further development and integration of the logistics and time sensitive freight operations in Australia and Asia and the existing American operations.
Mr. Mortimer intends to take up this appointment should the Offer be successful.
The combination of PTT Post, TNT and GD Express Worldwide is expected by KPN to generate greater opportunities overall for the employees of the operations involved.

Financing of the Offer KPN is financing the Offer and providing working capital facilities for the combined group by means of existing cash resources and a NLG 2.25 billion (A$1.7 billion) revolving credit facility, which has been arranged and fully underwritten by Goldman Sachs.
FURTHER INFORMATION
The Offer will be made by a wholly owned subsidiary of KPN, KPN (Australia) Limited.
It is expected that the documentation relating to the Offer will be dispatched to TNT shareholders on or about 14th October, 1996.
This documentation will include letters from the Chairmen of KPN and TNT, the Offer, the Part A statement from KPN and the Part B statement from TNT.

The Offer is subject to certain conditions, including acceptance for at least 90 per cent of shares under each of the ordinary and converting preference share offers, and the approval of appropriate regulatory authorities in relevant jurisdictions, including Australia and Europe.
In addition, the offers for the ordinary shares and converting preference shares are inter-dependent.

A summary of the conditions is contained in Appendix 1 to this announcement. Details of the manner in which the offers extend to holders of securities with conversion rights into TNT ordinary shares are contained in Appendix II.
The Boards of KPN and KPN (Australia) Limited are being advised by Goldman Sachs.
The Board of TNT is being advised by Macquarie Corporate Finance Limited.
